title: Ask when unsure
subject: Careers

thread_tags.line: Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
thread_tags.rationale: S: reflect on a task attempt and support needed. So: listen, ask and respond during a work task. IL: choose a response mode, ask for help or pause. MR: give a person time to understand and ask a question without ridicule.

label: Public edition
objective_verbatim: Ask a clear question when a work instruction is unclear.
display_objective: Ask a clear question when a work step is not clear.
approved_activity: Explore fictional job cards with a missing detail, such as which tray to use.
Rehearse asking for the detail, listen to the reply and show the next step.
calendar_note: Year A. 23–27 November 2026. One 40-minute lesson. No day or clock slot inferred. Week 7 is assessing.
where_this_leads: This helps me get the information I need to do a job.
unit: Following instructions and asking for clarity
accreditation: The qualification and the accredited unit: staff confirm any mapping from actual work. No criteria or completion are inferred.
assessment: Weeks 1–6 are formative. Week 7 is the assessing lesson. Keep actual responses, support, gaps and next steps in the evidence record.

sources.note: The owner-approved standalone Careers outline is the weekly teaching source. Combined workbook rows supply context rather than substitute weekly objectives.
Background on independence, recognising jobs and taking responsibility. Generic wording is used. The raw workbook is not redistributed.

authoring_provenance.note: Newly authored tasks from the owner-approved Careers outline. Workbook cells supply context only. Paper rehearsal tasks, job cards and fixed replies are newly authored.

external_sources.note: Approval, curriculum context, template and authored visual provenance.

evidence.description: The learner’s question, the reply understood and the action taken, with support recorded.
evidence.status: not prefilled; actual response and support to be recorded

routes.Supported: Supported: choose between a relevant and an unrelated question for card A, receive the reply, then place the circle in the correct tray.
routes.Independent: Independent: ask for the missing detail on cards A and B, show what each reply means and act on it.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: use card C, identify more than one missing detail and ask follow-up questions before packing the requested set.

vocab.definition: Use a question to find something out.
One small fact about the task.

cases.text: Put the circle card in a tray.
cases.next_step: Relevant question: Which tray? Fixed adult reply: Use tray 2. Expected action: one circle card in tray 2.

cases.judgement: Missing detail: how many square cards.
cases.next_step: Relevant question: How many squares? Fixed adult reply: Put two square cards in tray 1. Expected action: two squares in tray 1.

cases.judgement: Missing details: which shape, how many and which tray.
cases.next_step: Adult brief: one circle card in tray 1. Answer the detail asked: circle cards; one card; tray 1. The learner asks further questions until the next action is clear.

CAREERS-BUILD-A2-W04 · Year A · Week beginning 23 November 2026
Term theme: Identity & Belonging
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
Staff brief: 0 minutes.
Teacher: All worker profiles, job roles, employers and settings are fictional. Use only large paper cards and the supplied tray mats on a clear table. Adults prepare any cutting. No lifting, machinery, sharp tools or real workplace task is needed. Do not ask about body, family or private experiences. No names are required. Respect a pause or quiet response, with no forced partner work or public performance. A learner can query an unclear or unsafe instruction. Follow the setting’s safeguarding route if a concern is raised.

A work step is not clear. What could the worker ask?
Spot a missing fact in a job card. Ask a question and show the reply. Use the reply to take the next step.
CAREERS-BUILD-A2-W04-E1: The learner’s question, the reply understood and the action taken, with support recorded.

Print both evidence pages and the three support pages. Cut the three job cards from page 1, the question cards and four shape cards from page 2. Keep the two numbered tray mats and rehearsal sheet whole. Use one circle and two squares for the core tasks; the extra circle supports the number choice. Keep Staff Answers out of view during each first attempt. Prepare a separate model set. Read the cards without supplying the missing detail. No real job, employer or personal information is used.

A asks for the missing detail. B is unrelated; C proposes guessing. Accept another clear form such as Where should the circle go? A selected question or communication aid can meet the question target. The adult supplies the stated reply only after the learner has asked or selected the question. Then check understanding through pointing, restatement or action.

Supported: choose between a relevant and an unrelated question for card A, receive the reply, then place the circle in the correct tray. Independent: ask for the missing detail on cards A and B, show what each reply means and act on it. Aspire: use card C, identify more than one missing detail and ask follow-up questions before packing the requested set.

Use three minutes to spot the missing detail on a job card. Use six minutes for the learner to ask, hear or read the fixed adult reply, show understanding and carry out the action. Use three minutes to record the chain and try a further card or question. Every route captures at least one complete question, reply, understanding and action chain. Reset the tray mats between cards.
Read aloud, point, scribe exact words or use the usual communication aid. Record support without treating speech speed or handwriting as the target.

All worker profiles, job roles, employers and settings are fictional. Use only large paper cards and the supplied tray mats on a clear table. Adults prepare any cutting. No lifting, machinery, sharp tools or real workplace task is needed. Do not ask about body, family or private experiences. No names are required. Respect a pause or quiet response, with no forced partner work or public performance. A learner can query an unclear or unsafe instruction. Follow the setting’s safeguarding route if a concern is raised.

Keep the original job card, the learner’s exact or selected question, the actual adult reply, how understanding was shown and the resulting placement. Record any prompt or repeated reply. Pointing, restatement or accurate action can show understanding. Guessing the correct tray without asking does not demonstrate this objective. Independent and Aspire routes extend the number or complexity of cases; the core evidence remains one complete chain.

Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // self-edit · ? read back · R responded · E evidence in the evidence record. R requires Voice, Audience, a specific NS+ prompt and the learner response in their own colour. E is recorded only when actual work is banked. Record support and unfinished work. Blank forms and adult models are not learner evidence.

Space: calm seating and clear paper resources. Voice: choose a response mode, explain a check or ask for a detail. Audience: an adult listens, replies and allows time. Influence: record any change to support or the next task in response.

S: reflect on a task attempt and support needed. So: listen, ask and respond during a work task. IL: choose a response mode, ask for help or pause. MR: give a person time to understand and ask a question without ridicule.

Offer the authentic task question, adult reply and learner response to the Communication portfolio. Identify what changed after the exchange. Keep evidence of the learner’s own or selected wording, not only an adult model.

These are teaching guides. Record the learner’s actual response and support. The fictional worker cards do not describe real people, employers or vacancies.
Relevant question: Which tray? Fixed adult reply: Use tray 2. Expected action: one circle card in tray 2.
Missing detail: how many square cards.
Relevant question: How many squares? Fixed adult reply: Put two square cards in tray 1. Expected action: two squares in tray 1.
Missing details: which shape, how many and which tray.
Adult brief: one circle card in tray 1. Answer the detail asked: circle cards; one card; tray 1. The learner asks further questions until the next action is clear.

The job card says: put the circle in a tray. One fact is missing: which tray? The worker asks: which tray should be used? The adult replies: use tray 2. The worker points to tray 2 to check. Then the worker puts the circle in tray 2.

A asks for the missing detail. B is unrelated; C proposes guessing. Accept another clear form such as Where should the circle go? A selected question or communication aid can meet the question target. The adult supplies the stated reply only after the learner has asked or selected the question. Then check understanding through pointing, restatement or action.

Keep the original job card, the learner’s exact or selected question, the actual adult reply, how understanding was shown and the resulting placement. Record any prompt or repeated reply. Pointing, restatement or accurate action can show understanding. Guessing the correct tray without asking does not demonstrate this objective. Independent and Aspire routes extend the number or complexity of cases; the core evidence remains one complete chain.

Card A: answer Use tray 2 after a relevant question. Card B: answer Put two square cards in tray 1. Card C: the full brief is one circle card in tray 1, but reply only to the detail asked so the learner can ask again. Accept equivalent questions. Repeat the exact reply if requested and record the repeat as support. Reset all cards and trays between trials.

Asking for a needed detail is useful work behaviour. Guessing correctly is not the same as clarifying. Repeating words without showing their meaning is incomplete evidence. A clear question can be short, pointed to or made with an aid; fluent speech and public performance are not required.
